extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and institutions applying for NIDDK/NIH research grants
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIDDK guidance describing how funding applications are peer-reviewed, how applications are tracked, and the process and requirements for filing an appeal of a review decision. Covers study section assignment, priority ratings, and timing/format requirements for appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step peer review process
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted funding applications undergo a two-step peer review process by outside scientific experts: (1) review by a study section organized by NIH’s Center for Scientific Review or NIDDK which assigns numeric priority ratings; (2) approval of the study section's recommendations by the NIDDK's National Advisory Council (mandated by U.S. law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-step reviews are conducted by study sections (CSR or NIDDK-organized). Second-step is council-level secondary review and approval. This describes the overall workflow and that both steps are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority ratings based on scientific merit and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The study section will assign numeric priority ratings to applications based on their scientific merit and feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific criteria that inform these judgments are provided in the Notice of Funding Opportunity (FOA) for each grant; applicants should consult the FOA for the exact review criteria applicable to their application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use FOA-specific review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific criteria for review can be found in the funding announcement for your grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different grant mechanisms and FOAs may list explicit review criteria (e.g., significance, investigators, innovation, approach, environment). Applicants must follow the FOA guidance because review will be based on those stated criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study section assignment and correct assignment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: R01s, R21s, and SBIR applications are typically reviewed by NIH’s Center for Scientific Review; RFAs, Ks, Ts, Fs, Rs, P01s, U01, and U34 applications are typically reviewed by study sections organized by NIDDK staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you believe your application has been assigned to NIDDK for review in error, contact your Scientific Review Officer (SRO). SRO contact information is available on eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application tracking and Program Official (PO) assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Information specific to your application, including your Program Official assignment, will be posted to your eRA Commons account throughout its review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should monitor eRA Commons for status updates and PO assignment; the PO is the primary program contact who can explain options and study section recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals: consult Program Official before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are strongly advised to speak with the NIDDK Program Official responsible for the application before they submit an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PO can explain available options and often help the applicant understand the study section's recommendation; many issues can be resolved informally at this stage without a formal appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals: formal appeal letter requirements (follow NOT-OD-11-064)
rubrics_metrics.description: If issues cannot be resolved by discussion, submit a formal appeal letter following the process and guidance in NOT-OD-11-064. Appeal letters should be countersigned by the organization/business official and sent to the NIDDK PO assigned to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal letters must be received after the summary statement is released and within 30 days of the Council meeting where secondary review of the application occurs. Appeal letters received fewer than 30 calendar days before the applicable NIDDK Council meeting will likely be deferred to the next Council meeting for consideration.
